title: Koszul and quotient towers have the same limit
statement:
Let $X,\Lambda,I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ and $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Put $P_m=\Lambda/I^m$, and use $Q_m$ and its transitions from [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-koszul-completion]. For this assertion, both derived inverse limits are computed by the total right derived inverse-limit functor on strict towers of $\Lambda_X$-module complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its product-cone triangle gives a choice of the adic derived inverse limit [def-weil-pbc-adic-derived-inverse-limit]. Compute the two towers with one K-flat representative of $K$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Define $\kappa_K$ and $\operatorname{comp}_K$ [def-weil-pbc-completion-map] using the strict compatible maps induced respectively by $\Lambda\to Q_m$ (the degree-zero inclusion) and $\Lambda\to P_m$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$c_K:K^{\wedge,\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_m K_m$$
induced by the strict quotient augmentations $Q_m\to P_m$, and it satisfies $c_K\circ\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$.

proof.text: Set $A=\Lambda$ and $a_j=f_j$ in [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-koszul-augmentation-pro-zero]. Its augmentation is $\epsilon_m:Q_m\to\Lambda/I^m[0]=P_m[0]$, not the augmentation to $\Lambda/J_m$. It exists because $f_j^m\in I^m$, so the degree-zero quotient kills every differential into degree zero. The transition squares commute because every degree-zero Koszul transition is the identity and $P_{m+1}\to P_m$ is the quotient. The cited statement therefore gives, for each $m$, some $k\ge m$ with $C_k\to C_m$ zero in $D(\Lambda)$, where $C_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_m)$. No assertion about the proof of that node is used.

proof.text: The constant-presheaf functor on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ preserves kernels and cokernels sectionwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], its module sheafification is an exact additive functor $M\mapsto M_X$ from $\Lambda$-modules to $\Lambda_X$-modules. Termwise it consequently preserves quasi-isomorphisms, shifts and cones (the cone differential is the block matrix of the original differentials and map), so it induces a functor on derived categories that sends zero morphisms to zero morphisms. Apply it to $C_k\to C_m$: the strict sheafified cone tower $(C_m)_X$ has zero transitions at the same indices.

Choose one K-flat resolution $F\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and compute derived tensor using [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Ordinary total tensor with $F$ gives a strict map $v_m:F\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(Q_m)_X\to F\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(P_m)_X$ and its transition squares. Its cone identifies with $F\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(C_m)_X$: tensor distributes over the two cone summands, and the identification of the shifted source summand uses the sign $(-1)^p$ on a tensor with an element in degree $p$ of $F$. Since $F$ is K-flat, tensoring sends an acyclic cone to an acyclic complex; it thus sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induces an additive functor on the derived category, sending the zero transitions from step 2 to zero. The cone tower of $v$ is therefore pro-zero in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. These are strict models for the two derived-tensor towers, with no flatness assumption on $K$ or the quotient modules.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to $v$ on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$. Step 3 verifies exactly its zero-cone-transition hypothesis, hence $c_K=R\lim(v)$ is an isomorphism. For each quotient, specialize [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity morphism of the pro-etale topos and the ring map $\Lambda_X\to(P_m)_X$. Its total left derived module-pullback functor is the quotient derived tensor, computed on K-flat resolutions with flat terms. The quotient maps define natural transformations of the ordinary tensor functors by $1\otimes(P_b\to P_a)$; their squares with maps of resolutions commute before localization and hence after taking the left derived functors. For the Koszul tower, each $(Q_m)_X$ is a bounded finite free complex; filter it by degrees, so the graded tensor complexes are finite sums of shifts of the input complex. Tensoring a quasi-isomorphism with $(Q_m)_X$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, by induction on this finite filtration. A map between K-flat representatives commutes with $1_F\otimes\epsilon_m$ and with all transitions. These squares consequently descend to the derived categories, independently of the representatives, and applying the strict-tower derived-limit functor proves naturality in $K$. At each level the composite $\Lambda\to Q_m\xrightarrow{\epsilon_m}P_m$ is the quotient $\Lambda\to P_m$: on degree zero it sends $a$ to its residue class, and the source has no other degrees. Thus the two strict maps from the constant tower $F$ satisfy $v\circ u_{\mathrm{Kos}}=u_{\mathrm{quot}}$. Apply the functor $R\lim$ and precompose with the canonical map $K\to R\lim(\operatorname{const}K)$ used in the strict-tower units. Functoriality gives $c_K\circ\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$. This uses no choice of fillers between unrelated product-cone triangles.
